details.apply: Adopt the patch release and regenerate release notes or other release artifacts from canonical source records; replace plain-text issue descriptions with HTTPS issue or pull-request URLs.
details.changes: Release-note source records now require durable HTTPS references, safe rendering keeps them clickable, and detailLabels in the selected standard controls the visible labels for each selected detail field.
details.compatibility: The current packaged release-notes standard remains version 1; existing custom standards without detailLabels fall back to field IDs, while new or edited records must use HTTPS sources.
details.notes: The renderer never invents an issue URL from prose, and summaries/detail values remain escaped literal metadata.
details.problem: Release records could describe an issue in plain text, which rendered as an unlinked code span, while the renderer hard-coded reader-facing labels that were not controlled by the selected artifact standard.

changes.summary: Make release-note source links durable and visible detail labels standard-owned.

details.apply: Adopt the patch release and regenerate the hash-locked process surfaces; no consumer-specific Windows workaround is required.
details.changes: The managed child environment now preserves LOCALAPPDATA alongside the existing explicit Windows runtime variables, with regression coverage for the Python bootstrap boundary.
details.compatibility: Non-breaking for the current v1 lifecycle contract; Windows checks receive one additional documented runtime-resolution input and unrelated ambient variables remain excluded.
details.notes: The variable is forwarded only when present on the host and is included in the bounded runtime identity so affected evidence cannot be reused silently.
details.problem: The installed bounded Windows process profile dropped LOCALAPPDATA, so a consumer bootstrap could pass its direct tests but fail when launched through the managed execution environment.

changes.summary: Preserve the Windows user-local application context required by bounded Python checks.
